t.E503.agn: JECFA set a 'not limited' ADI for ammonium hydrogen carbonate in 1965 and, in its last evaluation in 1982, decided that a numerical ADI was not necessary ('not specified'). In the EU, as a Group I additive, it may be used at quantum satis (as much as needed).
t.E503.body: Ammonium enters the body's nitrogen metabolism; it is used to make substances such as glutamine, and the end product of this metabolism is urea.
t.E503.found.0: May be used at quantum satis (as much as needed) in many foods in the EU
t.E503.prod: It is produced by the chemical reaction of ammonium sulphate and calcium carbonate, or of ammonia and carbon dioxide.
t.E503.regx.0: ADI 'not specified' for ammonium hydrogen carbonate.
t.E503.regx.1: Group I additive; generally permitted at quantum satis (as much as needed).
t.E503.summary: Ammonium carbonates (baker's ammonia). Used as a raising agent in cookies and biscuits.
t.E503.what: Ammonium carbonate and ammonium bicarbonate; used as a raising agent and acidity regulator.
